query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Addition of a refractory metal element with a large atomic radius, such as Mo or Nb, to the FeCoNi alloy to form a high-entropy alloy with enhanced coercivity.
generation.intervention: Addition of Mo or Nb to form a high-entropy alloy with composition FeCoNiMo or FeCoNiNb
generation.conditions: The high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion and pinning of domain walls by the added refractory metal element
generation.mechanism: The large atomic radius of the added element creates lattice distortion, which pins domain walls and increases the coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiMo or FeCoNiNb high-entropy alloy will exhibit higher coercivity than the FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys
generation.boundary: The high-entropy alloy must have a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R and an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Mo or Nb to be added and the resulting microstructure of the high-entropy alloy are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare FeCoNiMo and FeCoNiNb high-entropy alloys with varying compositions and measure their coercive fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the FeCoNiMo or FeCoNiNb alloy is not higher than that of the FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys, the hypothesis is falsified
